source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which routine urinalysis finding is abnormal?
questions.rationale: Normal urine has no albumin; pH 4.5–8, SG 1.010–1.020, straw/amber color.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Normal Urine Values (PDF p. 381)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why are women more prone to cystitis than men?
questions.rationale: A short urethra close to the rectum allows ascending E. coli infection.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cystitis (PDF p. 381)
questions.quote: Female (shorter urethra, childbirth, anatomic proximity of urethra to rectum)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which teaching helps prevent recurrent cystitis?
questions.rationale: Void after intercourse, void frequently, hydrate, avoid irritants, wipe front to back.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cystitis Management (PDF p. 381)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which organism most commonly causes cystitis?
questions.rationale: Ascending E. coli infection is most common.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cystitis (PDF p. 381)
questions.quote: Usually caused by an ascending bacterial infection (E.coli)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Colicky pain radiating from the flank down to the genitalia suggests:
questions.rationale: Ureterolithiasis causes excruciating, wavelike pain radiating to thigh and genitalia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Urolithiasis (PDF p. 382)
questions.quote: radiating down the thigh to the genitalia

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is a key nursing action for a client with renal colic?
questions.rationale: Strain urine and save stones for analysis; force fluids about 3 L/day.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Urolithiasis Nursing (PDF p. 383)
questions.quote: Stain urine using gauze pad & save solid materials for analysis

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Allopurinol is prescribed for which type of kidney stone?
questions.rationale: Allopurinol lowers uric acid; a low-purine diet also helps.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Urolithiasis Management (PDF p. 383)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with uric acid stones should limit:
questions.rationale: Uric acid stones: low-purine diet; avoid anchovies, sardines, organ meats.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stone Types (PDF p. 382)
questions.quote: Anchovies, organ meat, whole grain, nuts, sardines

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which stone forms from urea-splitting bacteria?
questions.rationale: Struvite (alkaline) stones are associated with infection.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stone Types (PDF p. 382)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Nocturia, hesitancy, and weak urine stream in a 65-year-old man suggest:
questions.rationale: BPH constricts the urethra causing obstructive symptoms.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, BPH (PDF p. 383)
questions.quote: Decrease in force of urine steam

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Finasteride treats BPH by:
questions.rationale: 5-alpha reductase inhibition reduces glandular hyperplasia; terazosin relaxes smooth muscle.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, BPH Management (PDF p. 384)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After TURP, the drainage becomes bright red. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Increase continuous bladder irrigation flow to clear reddish drainage and prevent clots.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, TURP Care (PDF p. 384)
questions.quote: If drainage is reddish, increase flow rate

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why is sterile normal saline used for bladder irrigation after TURP?
questions.rationale: Hypotonic fluid can be absorbed, causing water intoxication.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, TURP Care (PDF p. 384)
questions.quote: Us a sterile NSS to prevent water intoxication

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which discharge instruction is appropriate after prostatectomy?
questions.rationale: Avoid straining, heavy lifting, prolonged sitting, and long trips; do Kegel exercises.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, TURP Discharge (PDF p. 384)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Fever, chills, flank pain, and CVA tenderness suggest:
questions.rationale: Kidney infection causes systemic signs and costovertebral tenderness.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pyelonephritis (PDF p. 385)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis typically follows a strep throat by:
questions.rationale: AGN appears 7–10 days after GABHS infection.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, AGN (PDF p. 385)
questions.quote: After 7 - 10 days after streptococcal throat infection

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the pathognomonic sign of acute glomerulonephritis?
questions.rationale: Periorbital edema with hematuria, hypertension, and oliguria.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, AGN (PDF p. 386)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which diet is ordered for acute glomerulonephritis?
questions.rationale: Restrict sodium, fluid, and protein; give carbohydrates liberally.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, AGN Management (PDF p. 386)
questions.quote: Dietary restriction of sodium, fluid & protein

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Massive proteinuria with anasarca indicates:
questions.rationale: Increased glomerular permeability causes massive protein loss and generalized edema.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nephrotic Syndrome (PDF p. 387)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Acute renal failure from severe hemorrhage and hypotension is classified as:
questions.rationale: Pre-renal: hypoperfusion; intra-renal: tissue damage; post-renal: obstruction.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Renal Failure (PDF p. 387)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Acute renal failure caused by an enlarged prostate is:
questions.rationale: Urinary tract obstruction causes post-renal failure.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acute Renal Failure (PDF p. 387)
